# A second target's Specs project from the same specs
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #108, sha256:3c721c88024915607488ecf887e3105e27e9ffcc077f41230790c22a7b840cc2). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; test generation only)
- **Milestone:** Tests first: spec to test is the reliable artifact
- **Source:** Product direction, 2026-10-27 (keep Phrase's own deterministic compilers; test-code generation first, then implementation code; the LLM-as-compiler path is a hypothesis measured alongside, not instead) and Decider D74 (Codex, Copilot, Grok Support-it). The measure-first cards (102, 103) stay ahead of these.
- **Depends on:** 106
- **Story:** As Dana, I want the same spec to produce an equivalent test in a second target language, so that the behaviour I specified is judged the same way wherever the code runs.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given orders.phrase, When it is compiled with a second adapter (TypeScript or Python, chosen by a Decider note in the card) at test generation only, Then it writes one test per spec in that language with the same inputs and the same expected outcome for returns, fails with, responds and succeeds
  2. Given a hand-written implementation of the orders.phrase phrases in that language, When the generated tests run, Then they pass, and a one-line mutation of that implementation makes at least one fail (a test shows both)
  3. Given the adapter contract, When the second adapter is added, Then the compiler core gains no knowledge of the target (the core project references no adapter, as card 040 asserts)

## Context

- Specs-only: no implementation emission, no endpoints beyond what the tests call in process. This un-pauses ONE slice of the adapters line; the other adapter cards (028, 029, 030) and the vocabulary line stay paused (Decider D74).
- Toolchain for the second language must already exist on the machine or the card is parked and the missing tool is named in the Needs-product-owner file.
